With a population getting close to 23 million people according to the 2023 US Census estimates,[[7]](#cite_note-2023CensusEst-7)[[12]](#cite_note-:1-12) Florida is the most populous state in the [Southeastern United States](/wiki/Southeastern_United_States "Southeastern United States"), and the second-most populous state in the [South](/wiki/Southern_United_States "Southern United States") behind [Texas](/wiki/Texas "Texas"). Within the United States, it contains the highest percentage of people over 65 (17.3%), and the 8th fewest people under 18 (21.9%).[[13]](#cite_note-13) Florida's population growth primarily comes from those moving to the state. The rate of natural change of births and deaths is "typically flat" and actually had negative natural population change in 2020.[[12]](#cite_note-:1-12) The 2022 US Census estimate found the largest age group moving to Florida were those from 60 and 69 years old with the second largest age group being those from 50 to 59 years old.[[14]](#cite_note-14)

This is a list of the best-selling [video games](/wiki/Video_games "Video games") worldwide, ranked up to 50th place by reported [software](/wiki/Software "Software") unit sales. Reliable sources are split as to whether the title of best-selling video game should belong to *[Tetris](/wiki/Tetris "Tetris")*, a 1988 multi-platform [puzzle video game](/wiki/Puzzle_video_game "Puzzle video game") created by [Alexey Pajitnov](/wiki/Alexey_Pajitnov "Alexey Pajitnov"), or to *[Minecraft](/wiki/Minecraft "Minecraft")*, a 2011 multi-platform [sandbox game](/wiki/Sandbox_game "Sandbox game") created by [Markus Persson](/wiki/Markus_Persson "Markus Persson") and developed by [Mojang Studios](/wiki/Mojang_Studios "Mojang Studios"). Some sources consider *Tetris* to be the best-selling video game by combining the sales of all of its different versions, totaling 520 million as of 2022, while others consider the best-selling video game to be *Minecraft*, which has sold 350 million copies as of 2025, rejecting the aggregation of each *Tetris* release.[[a]](#cite_note-Dispute-8) The closest competitor to either is *[Grand Theft Auto V](/wiki/Grand_Theft_Auto_V "Grand Theft Auto V")*, which has sold over 225 million copies. The best-selling single-platform game is *[Wii Sports](/wiki/Wii_Sports "Wii Sports")*, with nearly 83 million sales for the [Wii](/wiki/Wii "Wii") console.[[b]](#cite_note-WiiSports-9)

The 1998 game *[Snake](/wiki/Snake_(1998_video_game) "Snake (1998 video game)")* is estimated to have shipped on over 400 million devices,[[8]](#cite_note-10) but is not listed as it was preinstalled and freely accessible on [Nokia](/wiki/Nokia "Nokia") mobile phones. Another sales issue involves *[The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim](/wiki/The_Elder_Scrolls_V:_Skyrim "The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim")*, which game director [Todd Howard](/wiki/Todd_Howard "Todd Howard") claims has sold over 60 million copies,[[9]](#cite_note-11) is deemed contentious due to Howard's history of making exaggerated statements about his games for promotional purposes.[[10]](#cite_note-12)

[Super Bowl XXXII](/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXXII "Super Bowl XXXII") saw quarterback [John Elway](/wiki/John_Elway "John Elway") and running back [Terrell Davis](/wiki/Terrell_Davis "Terrell Davis") lead the Denver Broncos to an upset victory over the defending champion Packers, snapping the NFC's thirteen-year winning streak.[[75]](#cite_note-77) The following year, the Broncos defeated the [Atlanta Falcons](/wiki/Atlanta_Falcons "Atlanta Falcons") in [Super Bowl XXXIII](/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXXIII "Super Bowl XXXIII"), Elway's fifth Super Bowl appearance, his second NFL championship, and his final NFL game.[[76]](#cite_note-78) The back-to-back victories heralded a change in momentum in which AFC teams would win nine out of 12 Super Bowls. In the years between 1995 and 2018, five teams—the Steelers, Patriots, Broncos, [Baltimore Ravens](/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens"), and [Indianapolis Colts](/wiki/Indianapolis_Colts "Indianapolis Colts")—accounted for 22 of the 24 AFC Super Bowl appearances (including the last 16), with those same teams often meeting each other earlier in the playoffs. In contrast, the NFC saw a different representative in the Super Bowl every season from 2001 through 2010.[[77]](#cite_note-79)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/Patriots_on_offense_at_Super_Bowl_XXXIX_1.jpg/250px-Patriots_on_offense_at_Super_Bowl_XXXIX_1.jpg)](/wiki/File:Patriots_on_offense_at_Super_Bowl_XXXIX_1.jpg)

The [Larry O'Brien Championship Trophy](/wiki/Larry_O%27Brien_Championship_Trophy "Larry O'Brien Championship Trophy") is awarded annually to the winning team of the [NBA Finals](/wiki/NBA_Finals "NBA Finals"), the league's championship series that concludes the playoffs.

The NBA playoffs begin in April after the conclusion of the regular season and [play-in tournament](/wiki/NBA_play-in_tournament "NBA play-in tournament") with the top eight teams in each conference,[[133]](#cite_note-manning270-133) regardless of divisional alignment, competing for the league's championship title, the [Larry O'Brien Championship Trophy](/wiki/Larry_O%27Brien_Championship_Trophy "Larry O'Brien Championship Trophy"). [Seeds](/wiki/Seeding_(sports) "Seeding (sports)") are awarded in strict order of regular season record (with a tiebreaker system used as needed).

Having a higher seed offers several advantages. Since the first seed begins the playoffs playing against the eighth seed, the second seed plays the seventh seed, the third seed plays the sixth seed, and the fourth seed plays the fifth seed, having a higher seed typically means a team faces a weaker opponent in the first round. The team in each series with the better record has home-court advantage, including the First Round.

The league began using its current format, with the top eight teams in each conference advancing regardless of divisional alignment, in the 2015–16 season. Previously, the top three seeds went to the division winners.[[146]](#cite_note-146)

The playoffs follow a tournament format. Each team plays an opponent in a best-of-seven series, with the first team to win four games advancing into the next round, while the other team is eliminated from the playoffs. I

In October 2011, Nutter with [New Orleans](/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans") Mayor [Mitch Landrieu](/wiki/Mitch_Landrieu "Mitch Landrieu") created Cities United, an initiative to reducing African-American male on African-American male violence. Cities United works to prevent violence in a collaborative effort among mayors, foundations, national nonprofits, federal agencies and youth.[[36]](#cite_note-36)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/04/Mayor_Michael_A._Nutter_-_Flickr_-_Knight_Foundation.jpg/250px-Mayor_Michael_A._Nutter_-_Flickr_-_Knight_Foundation.jpg)](/wiki/File:Mayor_Michael_A._Nutter_-_Flickr_-_Knight_Foundation.jpg)

Nutter speaks to the Knight Foundation in 2012.

Nutter also initiated the Youth Violence Reduction Partnership. The YVRP includes the City Probation & Parole, the Police and the Philadelphia Anti-Drug Anti Violence Network working in targeted police districts to identify youth at risk of becoming involved in crime and providing them support through access to employment, education, mentoring, health care and drug treatment.[[35]](#cite_note-phila.gov-35)

The humid, subtropical air mass typically in place over the Smoky Mountains, coupled with [orographic lift](/wiki/Orographic_lift "Orographic lift"), produces large amounts of precipitation. Annual precipitation amounts range from 50–80 in (1,300–2,000 mm),[[23]](#cite_note-NWA_article-23) with heavy winter snowfall in the higher elevations.[[24]](#cite_note-weatherbook-24) [Flash flooding](/wiki/Flash_flood "Flash flood") often occurs after heavy rain.[[23]](#cite_note-NWA_article-23)

The average temperature difference between the mountains, such as [Newfound Gap](/wiki/Newfound_Gap "Newfound Gap") at 5,048 ft (1,539 m) above [MSL](/wiki/Sea_level "Sea level"), and the valleys at about 1,600 ft (488 m), is between 10–13 °F (5.6–7.2 °C) for highs, and between 3–6 °F (1.7–3.3 °C) for lows. The difference between high temperatures is similar to the [moist adiabatic lapse rate](/wiki/Lapse_rate#Moist_adiabatic_lapse_rate "Lapse rate") of 3.3 °F (1.8 °C) per 1,000 ft (300 m), while the smaller difference between low temperatures is the result of frequent [temperature inversions](/wiki/Inversion_(meteorology) "Inversion (meteorology)") developing in the morning, most often in autumn.[[25]](#cite_note-govtdoc-25)

Strong damaging winds of 80–100 mph (130–160 km/h) or higher occur a few times each year around the Smoky Mountains, mainly during the cool season from October to April, as a result of a phenomenon known as [mountain waves](/wiki/Lee_wave "Lee wave").[[26]](#cite_note-govtwebpage-26) Mountain waves are strongest in a narrow area along the foothills and can create extensive areas of fallen trees and roof damage, especially around Cades Cove and Cove Mountain.[[27]](#cite_note-WAFarticle-27) Strong winds created by mountain waves were a contributing factor in the devastating Gatlinburg fire on November 28, 2016, during the [2016 Great Smoky Mountains wildfires](/wiki/2016_Great_Smoky_Mountains_wildfires "2016 Great Smoky Mountains wildfires").[[28]](#cite_note-28) Damaging winds can also be generated by strong [thunderstorms](/wiki/Thunderstorms "Thunderstorms"), with [torn

With more than 2.4 million inhabitants as of 2020, it is the most populous municipality in the Northeast, the fifth most populous in Brazil, and the ninth largest Latin American city. It is the core of the [metropolitan area](/wiki/Metropolitan_area "Metropolitan area") known as "Great Salvador", which had an estimated 3,957,123 inhabitants in 2020 according to the [Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics](/wiki/Brazilian_Institute_of_Geography_and_Statistics "Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics") (IBGE). This makes it the second most populous metropolitan area in the Northeast, the [seventh in Brazil](/wiki/List_of_metropolitan_areas_in_Brazil "List of metropolitan areas in Brazil"), and one of the [largest in South America](/wiki/List_of_South_American_metropolitan_areas_by_population "List of South American metropolitan areas by population"). Also due to these urban-population dimensions, it is classified by the IBGE study on the [Brazilian urban network](/wiki/Urban_hierarchy_in_Brazil "Urban hierarchy in Brazil") as a regional [metropolis](/wiki/Metropolis "Metropolis"). In its reports for the years 2014 and 2020, the Research Network of Globalization and World Cities (GaWC) classified Salvador as a [global city](/wiki/Global_city "Global city") in the "Sufficiency" category (the smallest). Global city surveys by consultancy Kearney also included Salvador in the 2018 and 2020 annual reports, while excluding it in the 2019.

The economic center of the state, Salvador is also a [port city](/wiki/Port_city "Port city"), administrative and tourist center. Its metropolitan region has the highest GDP among urban concentrations in the Northeast. In 2018, it had the second-highest [gross domestic product](/wiki/Gross_domestic_product "Gross domestic product") (GDP) among Northeastern municipalities. Furthermore, it is the headquarters of important regional, national and international companies, such as [Novonor](/wiki/Novonor "Novonor"), [Braskem](/wiki/Braskem "Braskem"), Neoenergy Coelba, and [Suzano Papel e Celulose](/wiki/Suzano_Papel_e_Celulose "Suzano Papel e Celulose"). After practicing [internal medicine](/wiki/Internal_medicine "Internal medicine") as a [chief physician](/wiki/Chief_physician "Chief physician") at two hospitals, he won election in 1996 to represent [Tainan City](/wiki/Tainan_City "Tainan City") in the [National Assembly](/wiki/National_Assembly_(Republic_of_China) "National Assembly (Republic of China)"), then served in the [Legislative Yuan](/wiki/Legislative_Yuan "Legislative Yuan") from 1999 to 2010. Skulls of African bush elephant (left) and African forest elephant (right)

The African forest elephant is considerably smaller than the African bush elephant, though the size of the species has been subject to contradictory estimates. A 2000 study suggested that bulls of the species reach a shoulder height of 2.4–3 m (7.9–9.8 ft), and weighed 4–7 t (4.4–7.7 short tons), while cows were about 1.8–2.4 m (5.9–7.9 ft) tall at the shoulder and 2–4 t (2.2–4.4 short tons).[[4]](#cite_note-Grubb_al2000-4) However, a 2003 study of forest elephants at a reserve in Gabon did not find any elephants taller than 2.16 m (7.1 ft).[[12]](#cite_note-12) A 2015 study alternately suggested that fully grown African forest elephant males in optimal condition were only on average 2.2 m (7.2 ft) tall and 2 t (2.2 short tons) in weight, with the largest individuals (representing less than 1 in 100,000 as a proportion of the total population) no bigger than 2.75 m (9.0 ft) tall and 3.5 t (3.9 short tons) in weight.[[13]](#cite_note-probos_mass-13)

The African forest elephant has grey skin, which looks yellow to reddish after [wallowing](/wiki/Wallowing "Wallowing"). It is sparsely covered with black coarse hair, which is 20–200 mm (0.8–8 in) long around the tip of the tail. The length of the tail varies between individuals from half the height of the rump to almost touching ground. Tomas Tranströmer :: Life and work :: Poetry :: chunk_0002
Tranströmer is considered to be one of the "most influential Scandinavian poet[s] of recent decades".[[5]](#cite_note-ap_nobel-5) Tranströmer published 15 collected works over his extensive career, which have been translated into over 60 languages.[[5]](#cite_note-ap_nobel-5) An English translation by [Robin Fulton](/wiki/Robin_Fulton "Robin Fulton") of his entire body of work, *New Collected Poems*, was published in the UK in 1987 and expanded in 1997. Following the publication of *The Great Enigma*, Fulton's edition was further expanded into *The Great Enigma: New Collected Poems,* published in the US in 2006 and as an updated edition of *New Collected Poems*[[9]](#cite_note-9) in the UK in 2011. He published a short autobiography, *Minnena ser mig* *(The Memories see me)*, in 1993.

By the mid-1960s, Tranströmer became close friends with poet [Robert Bly](/wiki/Robert_Bly "Robert Bly"). The two corresponded frequently, and Bly translated Tranströmer's poems into English. In 2001 [Bonniers](/wiki/Bonnier_Group "Bonnier Group"), Tranströmer's publisher, released *Air Mail*, a work consisting of Tranströmer's and Bly's day-to-day correspondence on personal, contemporary and literary matters c. 1965–1991 – in a style that vividly conveyed how close friends the two had soon become.[[5]](#cite_note-ap_nobel-5) Bly also helped arrange readings for his fellow poet in America. The Syrian poet [Adunis](/wiki/Adunis "Adunis") helped spread Tranströmer's fame in the [Arab world](/wiki/Arab_world "Arab world"), accompanying him on reading tours.[[10]](#cite_note-10)

In the 1970s, other poets accused Tranströmer of being detached from his own age, since he did not deal overtly with social and political issues in his poems and novels. His work, though, lies within and further develops the [Modernist](/wiki/Modernist "Modernist") and [Expressionist](/wiki/Expressionist "Expressionist")/[Surrealist](/wiki/Surrealist "Surrealist") language of 20th-century poetry; his clear, seemingly simple pictures from everyday life and nature, in particular, reveals a mystic insight to the universal aspects of the human mind.

The Foldex cat, also known as the Exotic Fold, is a cat breed developed in the [Canadian](/wiki/Canada "Canada") province of [Quebec](/wiki/Quebec "Quebec") by crossbreeding a [Scottish Fold](/wiki/Scottish_Fold "Scottish Fold") and an [Exotic Shorthair](/wiki/Exotic_Shorthair "Exotic Shorthair"). Foldexes are medium-sized cats with a rounded face, short legs, and sometimes folded ears; while the latter are intended to be the defining feature of the breed, only about 50% of them exhibit it. The eyes are rounded, the ears small, and the body stout like that of Scottish Fold, with a short face between those of the two originating breeds. The coat may be of any length, colour, and pattern.[[29]](#cite_note-CCA_std-29) The variety is recognized as a breed in its own right by one [cat registry](/wiki/Cat_registry "Cat registry"), the [Canadian Cat Association](/wiki/Canadian_Cat_Association "Canadian Cat Association") (CCA),[[29]](#cite_note-CCA_std-29)[[30]](#cite_note-ShowCatsOnline-30) but not by any of the major international ones.[[29]](#cite_note-CCA_std-29) Foldexes have genetic predispositions to multiple medical disorders, primarily inherited from the Scottish Fold, and their breeding has been banned in some countries as a result.

In 1995, a Foldex was first exhibited in a [cat show](/wiki/Cat_show "Cat show") by breed Betty-Ann Yaxley in [Quebec](/wiki/Quebec "Quebec"). Kagan was born and raised in New York City. After graduating from [Princeton University](/wiki/Princeton_University "Princeton University"), [Worcester College, Oxford](/wiki/Worcester_College,_Oxford "Worcester College, Oxford"), and [Harvard Law School](/wiki/Harvard_Law_School "Harvard Law School"), she clerked for a federal Court of Appeals judge and for Supreme Court Justice [Thurgood Marshall](/wiki/Thurgood_Marshall "Thurgood Marshall"). She began her career as a professor at the [University of Chicago Law School](/wiki/University_of_Chicago_Law_School "University of Chicago Law School"), leaving to serve as Associate [White House Counsel](/wiki/White_House_Counsel "White House Counsel"), and later as a policy adviser under [President](/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") [Bill Clinton](/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton"). After a nomination to the [United States Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit](/wiki/United_States_Court_of_Appeals_for_the_District_of_Columbia_Circuit "United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit"), which expired without action, she became a professor at [Harvard Law School](/wiki/Harvard_Law_School "Harvard Law School") and was later named its first female [dean](/wiki/Dean_(education) "Dean (education)").

In 2009, Kagan became the first female [solicitor general of the United States](/wiki/Solicitor_General_of_the_United_States "Solicitor General of the United States").[[2]](#cite_note-2) The following year, President Obama [nominated her](/wiki/Elena_Kagan_Supreme_Court_nomination "Elena Kagan Supreme Court nomination") to the Supreme Court to fill the vacancy arising from the impending retirement of Justice [John Paul Stevens](/wiki/John_Paul_Stevens "John Paul Stevens"). The [United States Senate](/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate") confirmed her nomination by a vote of 63–37. As of 2022, she is the most recent justice appointed without any prior judicial experience. Main article: [Demographics of Russia](/wiki/Demographics_of_Russia "Demographics of Russia")

See also: [List of cities and towns in Russia by population](/wiki/List_of_cities_and_towns_in_Russia_by_population "List of cities and towns in Russia by population")

Russia had a population of 141.18 million according to the [2010 census](/wiki/Russian_Census_(2010) "Russian Census (2010)"),[[11]](#cite_note-2010Census-16) which rose to 146.2 million as of 2021 following the [annexation of Crimea](/wiki/Annexation_of_Crimea_by_the_Russian_Federation "Annexation of Crimea by the Russian Federation") in 2014.[[12]](#cite_note-17) It is the [most populous country](/wiki/List_of_European_countries_by_population "List of European countries by population") in Europe, and the [ninth-most populous country](/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population "List of countries and dependencies by population") in the world; with a [population density](/wiki/List_of_countries_by_population_density "List of countries by population density") of 9 inhabitants per square kilometre (23 inhabitants/mi2).[[13]](#cite_note-18)
